{"candidate_slot":1,"current_prompt":"You are given a JSON input with two parts:

1. `system_profile`: the installed software inventory. Each entry lists a product name (which may be a package-manager name, a repo-style component name, or a title-cased product name), the installed version, and possibly other metadata.
2. `advisories`: a list of CVE advisories. Each advisory contains a unique CVE identifier, a description, and `affected` information describing vulnerable products and version constraints.

Your job: identify which supplied advisories apply to the installed system and return ONLY a JSON object {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} containing unique advisory IDs copied exactly from the supplied list, or {"applicable_cves":[]} if none apply.

CRITICAL — BE LIBERAL AND EXHAUSTIVE. Your known failure mode is MISSING applicable advisories. Every advisory whose product is installed and whose version falls in ANY affected range must be included. Do not exclude an advisory merely because the product name looks stylistically different (underscores vs spaces, hyphens vs dots), the description is long, or you are uncertain. Include the advisory whenever product and version matching both succeed. Bias toward coverage: when product identity is plausible and the version satisfies the range, INCLUDE it. Only exclude an advisory when (a) the product is clearly NOT installed under any alias, or (b) the installed version is unambiguously outside EVERY affected range, or (c) the product name is superficially similar but genuinely a different product (e.g., `libjpeg` vs `libjpeg-turbo`, `json-c` vs `jsmn`, `openssl` vs `openssh`).

Matching rules:

1. PRODUCT MATCHING — liberal. An advisory is a candidate if any affected product matches an installed product. Names may appear as package-manager identifiers (`libxml2`, `openssl`), repo/component names (`node`, `chromium`), or title-cased vendor names (`OpenSSL`, `Libxml2`, `Chromium`). Normalize case, separators (hyphens/underscores/dots/spaces — treat `open_ssl`, `open-ssl`, `OpenSSL`, and `open ssl` as identical), and common abbreviations before comparing. Also handle vendor-stripped aliases: an advisory may name a product with the vendor prefix removed or added (e.g., installed `libjpeg-turbo` vs advisory `libjpeg`; advisory `OpenSSL` vs installed `openssl`). Check the advisory description text for alternate product names — the affected product may be named there even when the `affected` field uses a different alias. Consider ALL installed products; do not stop at the first match attempt.

2. VERSION MATCHING — precise and inclusive-leaning. For each candidate, parse the affected range from the `affected` data (structured objects with `introduced`, `fixed`, `last_affected`, `less_than`, `less_than_or_equal`, `version`, `versions`) AND from prose in the description ('versions prior to 1.2.3', 'affected 4.5.6 and later before 5.0', 'through 2.1', 'up to and including 3.0').
   - Compare versions NUMERICALLY, segment by segment, padding missing trailing segments with zero as needed (installed `2.5` vs fixed `2.5.1` → 2.5.0 < 2.5.1, so affected; 1.10 > 1.9; installed `1.2` vs fixed `1.2.1` → vulnerable). NEVER compare versions as strings ('10' < '9' is FALSE numerically).
   - `introduced` is INCLUSIVE (that version is vulnerable). `fixed` and `less_than` are EXCLUSIVE (that version is safe). `last_affected` and `less_than_or_equal` are INCLUSIVE (that version is vulnerable).
   - Prose: 'before'/'prior to' = exclusive; 'through'/'up to and including' = inclusive; 'and later'/'from X' = inclusive lower bound.
   - BOUNDARY RULE: if the installed version equals an INCLUSIVE bound (`introduced`, `last_affected`, `less_than_or_equal`, or a 'through'/'up to and including' bound), it IS affected — include the advisory. If it equals an EXCLUSIVE bound (`fixed`, `less_than`, or a 'before'/'prior to' bound), it is NOT affected. A version exactly at `last_affected` is a very common miss — double-check these.
   - If the installed version is BELOW an upper bound (e.g., below `fixed`) and at/above any lower bound, include it — a very common miss is installed versions positioned below the fixed version. Likewise, installed versions ABOVE a stated lower bound with no upper bound ('from 3.2 and later') must be included, even when the installed version has more segments or is much newer. If installed is at/above `introduced` and below `fixed`, include it even when segment counts differ (4-segment installed vs 3-segment fixed, etc.) — pad and compare numerically.
   - An advisory may list multiple affected ranges or multiple affected products; it is applicable if the installed version falls in ANY one range for ANY matched product. Check EVERY listed range, not just the first.
   - If a range says 'all versions', or `version: 'all'`, any installed version matches.

3. APPLICABILITY. Include an advisory only when BOTH (a) a product in its affected list matches an installed product under normalization/aliasing, and (b) the installed version satisfies at least one vulnerable range for that product. If the product is not installed at all, exclude. If the product is installed but the version is outside every range, exclude. Otherwise include.

4. OUTPUT DISCIPLINE.
   - Return ONLY the JSON object {"applicable_cves":[...]} — no explanations, no markdown, no code fences, no extra keys or text. The entire response must be valid JSON starting with `{` and ending with `}`.
   - Include every advisory that passes product + version matching; copy IDs verbatim from the supplied list with correct year and sequence digits. Each ID at most once; order does not matter.
   - If no advisory applies, return {"applicable_cves":[]} exactly.

Work through EVERY supplied advisory one by one — never skip any. For each: (1) scan all installed products for a name match after normalization and alias handling, including vendor-stripped forms, underscore/space/hyphen variants, and names mentioned in the description; (2) if matched, locate EVERY affected range (structured and prose) and evaluate the installed version against it with correct inclusive/exclusive semantics; (3) include the advisory if any range is satisfied. Before finalizing, re-verify: inclusive boundaries (at `last_affected`/`introduced`), below-fixed-version cases, above-lower-bound-no-upper cases, and multi-segment comparisons — these are where misses occur
